status: DEMONSTRATION MODEL — NOT YET VALIDATED FOR OFFICIAL PLANNING USE
validation_notes: The variables, membership breakpoints, rule weights, and category thresholds are demonstration assumptions.
Qualified specialists in flood hazards, engineering geology, seismology, disaster-risk reduction, and land-use planning must review and validate this configuration before operational use.
Historical incidents and CLUP references are displayed as decision context; they are not numerical fuzzy inputs in this model version.
An unavailable required input produces an incomplete assessment. It is never converted to zero or interpreted as low vulnerability.
ULAP classification-to-index transformations below are transparent capstone assumptions and require validation by qualified MGB, PHIVOLCS, DRRM, geotechnical, and planning specialists.
Official ULAP codes and labels remain unchanged in the source result; the separate normalized index is used only by the GeoSafe-FIS fuzzy model.

inputs.name: Flood susceptibility
inputs.description: Normalized screening representation of the available flood classification at the selected point.

normalization.method: Exact code lookup from the verified live domain; the official label is preserved separately.
normalization.missing_value_policy: An absent feature, missing field, changed schema, or unknown code remains missing and makes the assessment incomplete.
normalization.validation_requirement: DEMONSTRATION TRANSFORMATION — the four model index values require review and approval by qualified domain experts before official planning use.

inputs.name: Liquefaction susceptibility
inputs.description: Normalized screening representation of the available liquefaction classification at the selected point.

normalization.source_domain: Live ArcGIS coded-value domain containing two distinct classification families
normalization.method: Exact code lookup configured independently for every official category; no ordinal sequence is inferred from the code numbers.

01.note: Broad legacy/general category; deliberately not treated as Low Potential.

normalization.missing_value_policy: An absent feature, missing field, changed schema, or unknown code remains missing and makes the assessment incomplete.
normalization.validation_requirement: DEMONSTRATION TRANSFORMATION — these non-equivalent source categories and all seven model index values require PHIVOLCS/domain-expert validation before official planning use.

inputs.name: Ground-shaking intensity
inputs.description: Normalized screening representation of the available ground-shaking classification at the selected point.

normalization.method: No transformation is configured until an authorized ground-shaking layer, field, unit, classification system, and domain are verified.
normalization.missing_value_policy: Ground shaking remains unavailable; do not substitute Active Fault, distance to fault, epicenters, liquefaction, or an invented intensity.
normalization.validation_requirement: A verified ground-shaking endpoint and a domain-expert-approved source-to-model transformation are required before a three-hazard score can be calculated.

rules.statement: IF flood is high AND liquefaction is high AND ground shaking is high THEN vulnerability is very high
rules.rationale: Concurrent strong evidence across all three hazards warrants the strongest screening output.

rules.statement: IF flood is high AND liquefaction is high THEN vulnerability is very high
rules.rationale: Two co-located high hazard classifications materially increase planning concern.

rules.statement: IF flood is high AND ground shaking is high THEN vulnerability is very high
rules.rationale: Two co-located high hazard classifications materially increase planning concern.

rules.statement: IF liquefaction is high AND ground shaking is high THEN vulnerability is very high
rules.rationale: Strong shaking combined with high liquefaction susceptibility is a critical coupled signal.

rules.statement: IF any required hazard is high THEN vulnerability is high
rules.rationale: A single high hazard remains planning-significant even when the other inputs are lower.

rules.statement: IF flood is moderate AND liquefaction is moderate AND ground shaking is moderate THEN vulnerability is moderate
rules.rationale: Consistent mid-range evidence supports a moderate screening result.

rules.statement: IF flood is moderate AND liquefaction is moderate THEN vulnerability is moderate
rules.rationale: Two moderate classifications reinforce a moderate multi-hazard signal.

rules.statement: IF flood is moderate AND ground shaking is moderate THEN vulnerability is moderate
rules.rationale: Two moderate classifications reinforce a moderate multi-hazard signal.

rules.statement: IF liquefaction is moderate AND ground shaking is moderate THEN vulnerability is moderate
rules.rationale: Two moderate classifications reinforce a moderate multi-hazard signal.

rules.statement: IF any required hazard is moderate THEN vulnerability is moderate
rules.rationale: A moderate hazard should remain visible in the combined screening output.

rules.statement: IF flood is low AND liquefaction is low AND ground shaking is low THEN vulnerability is low
rules.rationale: Only available evidence consistently classified as low strongly supports the low output.

rules.statement: IF any required hazard is low THEN vulnerability is low
rules.rationale: Low evidence contributes cautiously without overriding stronger hazard evidence.

Low: Maintain current risk-reduction measures and verify site-specific conditions before committing land-use or capital decisions.
Keep hazard and incident records current; a low screening result does not mean no hazard.
Moderate: Include the location in more detailed planning review and compare the result with current official hazard maps.
Consider site inspection and appropriate professional advice before approving sensitive or high-occupancy uses.
High: Prioritize detailed site-specific hazard assessment and risk-reduction options before major planning or investment decisions.
Review applicable evacuation, drainage, structural, and land-use controls with qualified municipal and technical personnel.
Very High: Treat the location as a priority for detailed multi-hazard investigation and cautious land-use review.
Avoid using this screening result alone to approve development; obtain current official assessments and qualified technical advice.
Incomplete: Do not infer low vulnerability. Obtain the missing required hazard information and run the assessment again.
Use available incident and CLUP context only as supporting information, not as a substitute for missing hazard inputs.

disclaimer: This output is a preliminary decision-support screening result based on the availability and classifications of the cited source datasets. It is not an official hazard certification, zoning approval, building-safety rating, structural assessment, engineering recommendation, or disaster forecast.
